overview: This Senate resolution designates the week of April 19 through April 27, 2025, as "National Park Week." It notes that Congress created Yellowstone, the first national park, in 1872 and the National Park Service, the federal agency that runs the parks, in 1916. It highlights that the parks drew nearly 332 million recreational visits in 2024 and that visitor spending supports the economy, and it praises park employees. The resolution encourages people to responsibly visit and support national parks. It does not change park funding or rules. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on April 10, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution celebrates places that preserve the nation's natural and historic heritage and encourages more people to enjoy them.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or provide funding for the parks or their staff.
